newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate inches up on primary rate hike.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate inches up on primary rate hike.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed up 10 basis points at 23.30 percent on Wednesday under the influence of an uptick in primary rates amid quiet dealing, traders said.
"Nothing happened in the market, rates traded within a very narrow range," a trader said.
"The secondary market absorbed the 47-basis point rise in bellwether 28-day Cetes rates and that's why the market closed up. Otherwise, there was nothing to move it," a money market analyst said.
Traders said the rise in secondary rates was moderate due to a firm peso and a relatively stable U.S. long bond.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts closed 1.5 centavos firmer at 7.8870/7.8890 per dollar, while the U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was down 1/32 to yield 7.10 percent.
Overnight rates on bank paper closed unchanged at 25.00 percent.
Mild inflation figures released in late trade also helped contain the increase in secondary market rates, traders said.

Banco de Mexico said consumer prices in March rose 1.24 percent, down from 1.68 percent in February. The market was looking for an average increase of 1.31 percent, according to a Reuters survey of Mexico City financial houses.
The central bank drained 6.841 billion pesos through seven auctions, which it assigned at rates of 25.14-25.41 percent.
Liquidity of 5.577 billion pesos was slated to return to the system from prior central bank operations.
